HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2023-07-15
Provider: Dr. Emily Thompson, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Progressive weakness in legs and difficulty walking with tingling in feet for 1 week

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 35-year-old male with HIV, chronic hepatitis B and C, opioid use disorder, and recent hospitalizations for infective endocarditis and psoas abscess, who presents with progressive weakness in his legs and difficulty walking for one week. He also reports tingling sensations in his feet.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Acute hepatitis B virus infection (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- HIV-related opportunistic skin infection (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Molluscum contagiosum (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
- Membranous glomerulonephritis (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
- Psoas abscess (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
- Infective Endocarditis (Aortic Valve) with Complications (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
- Human immunodeficiency virus infection
- Chronic hepatitis C virus infection
- Opioid use disorder (intravenous)

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Non-contributory

SOCIAL HISTORY:
He has a past medical history of intravenous drug use and unprotected sexual encounters with multiple partners. He has not been tested for HIV.

VITAL SIGNS:
Vital signs are stable, and there are no signs of respiratory distress.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the patient has bilateral lower extremity weakness, areflexia, and decreased sensation in a glove-and-stocking distribution.

LABORATORY DATA:
Initial laboratory tests are as follows:

- Complete blood count: within normal limits
- Comprehensive metabolic panel: within normal limits
- Erythrocyte sedimentation rate: 20 mm/hr (normal < 15 mm/hr)
- HIV antibody/antigen test: Positive

OTHER STUDIES:
Nerve conduction studies show slowed conduction velocities and prolonged distal latencies consistent with demyelination. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis reveals an elevated protein level with a normal white blood cell count.
